mainTopic: The wonderful fertility of ארץ ישראל and the חכמים' love for the land
overview: This amud continues the גמרא's praise of ארץ ישראל and its amazing fruit. Three חכמים are served a peach as big as a large pot. A year later רבי אלעזר finds it has shrunk to fit in his hand, and he blames the people's sins. רבי יהושע בן לוי sees grape clusters as big as calves and tells the land to hold back its fruit from the גוים who rule over ישראל. A ברייתא then compares yields: even rocky חברון was seven times better than צוען, the best land in מצרים, and in a blessed year the land gave fifty thousand כור. More stories follow: a צדוקי praises his small field, and a palm tree by the ירדן still gives its full yield. רב חסדא explains why the land is called a צבי. The amud ends with חכמים who showed their love for the land: רבי אלעזר escaping three curses, רבי זירא rushing across the river, רבי אבא kissing its rocks, and רבי חנינא fixing its roads. The story of רבי אמי and רבי אסי begins and continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The size of the land flowing with milk and honey
steps.stepSummary: The previous statement ends by giving the size of the area: 22 פרסאות long and 6 פרסאות wide, like the stretch from בי מיכסי to the fortress of תולבנקי.
steps.simpleTranslation: And it was the size of the area from Bei Mikhsei to the fortress of Tulbanki: twenty-two parasangs long and six parasangs wide.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a statement that began on the previous amud. It gives the size of the area in ארץ ישראל that flowed with milk and honey.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The speaker compares the land's 'milk and honey' area to a well-known stretch of land so listeners can picture it. The point is that the land's richness covered a huge area.

keyTerms.meaning: Parasangs, a unit of distance (about 4 מילין each)

phrases.english: And it was like the area from Bei Mikhsei
until the fortress of Tulbanki,
twenty-two parasangs in length
and six parasangs in width.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes a statement begun on the previous amud.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The milk-and-honey area of the land measured 22 by 6 פרסאות.

steps.title: Three sages are served a giant peach
steps.stepSummary: רבי חלבו, רבי עוירא and רבי יוסי בר חנינא came to a certain place and were served a peach as big as a stewpot of כפר הינו.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חלבו, רבי עוירא and רבי יוסי בר חנינא happened to come to a certain place. They brought before them a peach that was as big as a stewpot of כפר הינו.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new story showing how big the fruit of ארץ ישראל used to be.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The peach is compared to a known stewpot size from the town of כפר הינו. This sets up the next question: how big is that pot?

keyTerms.meaning: A town known for a certain size of pot

phrases.english: Rabbi Chelbo and Rabbi Avira
and Rabbi Yosei bar Chanina
happened to come to a certain place.
They brought before them a peach
that was like a stewpot of Kefar Hino.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי חֶלְבּוֹ וְרַבִּי עַוִּירָא וְרַבִּי יוֹסֵי בַּר חֲנִינָא אִיקְּלַעוּ לְהָהוּא אַתְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new story in the same series praising the land's fruit.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The fruit of ארץ ישראל was once enormous; a single peach was as big as a large pot.

steps.title: How big is a stewpot of כפר הינו?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא stops the story to ask how big the stewpot of כפר הינו actually is.
steps.simpleTranslation: And how big is a stewpot of כפר הינו?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a simple clarifying question so we understand the size of the peach.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is not a challenge. Without knowing the size of the pot, the comparison would mean nothing to us.

phrases.english: And a stewpot of Kefar Hino, how much is it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about the size mentioned in step 2.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The capacity of the stewpot of כפר הינו.

steps.title: The pot holds five סאין
steps.stepSummary: The answer: the stewpot holds five סאין.
steps.simpleTranslation: Five סאין.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the pot held five סאין, which is a very large amount.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now we know the peach was huge, about the size of a pot holding five סאין.

phrases.english: Five se'ah.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 3.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The pot of כפר הינו holds five סאין.

steps.title: The sages split the peach three ways
steps.stepSummary: The sages ate a third, made a third הפקר, and gave a third to their animals.
steps.simpleTranslation: They ate a third, declared a third ownerless, and placed a third before their animals.
steps.whatsHappening: The story goes on: one peach was so big that three people could not finish it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even after eating, there was enough left to give away and to feed their animals. This shows just how large the fruit was.

keyTerms.meaning: They declared it ownerless (הפקר), free for anyone to take

phrases.english: They ate a third, and declared a third ownerless,
and placed a third before their animals.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the story after the side question about the pot.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The peach was so large that it was split three ways and still went beyond what they could eat.

steps.title: A year later the peach has shrunk
steps.stepSummary: The next year רבי אלעזר came to the same place, and the peach fit in his hand. He quoted a פסוק saying a fruitful land turns to salt because of the people's sins.
steps.simpleTranslation: The next year רבי אלעזר happened to come there, and they brought him a peach. He held it in his hand and said: 'A fruitful land into a salt waste, because of the wickedness of those who live there.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא contrasts the earlier story. One year later the same kind of fruit fit in one hand, and רבי אלעזר explained why.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The change from a pot-sized peach to a hand-sized one is blamed on sin, using a פסוק from תהלים. The land's blessing depends on how the people behave.
steps.whatToRemember: The great fruit of ארץ ישראל is not guaranteed. When the people sin, the land's blessing shrinks.

phrases.english: The next year, Rabbi Elazar happened to come there
and they brought it before him.
He held it in his hand, and said:
phrases.notes: Some versions have the word in round brackets; the word in square brackets is the corrected wording, 'he held it.'

phrases.english: "A fruitful land into a salt waste,"
"because of the wickedness of those who live in it."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Contrasts with the giant peach of the year before.
steps.whyThisMatters: It turns a story of wonder into a lesson: the land's blessing depends on the people's deeds.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Sin causes the fruit of the land to shrink.

steps.title: רבי יהושע בן לוי sees 'calves' among the vines
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע בן לוי came to גבלא, saw grape clusters as big as calves, and asked why calves were standing among the vines.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהושע בן לוי happened to come to Gavla. He saw clusters of grapes standing like calves, and said: Calves among the vines?
steps.whatsHappening: A new story begins. רבי יהושע בן לוי thinks he sees calves in a vineyard and asks about it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The clusters were so huge that from a distance they looked like young cows. His question sets up the surprising answer in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: Gavla, a place in the north of ארץ ישראל

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי אִיקְּלַע לְגַבְלָא,
phrases.english: Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi happened to come to Gavla,
he saw those clusters
that were standing like calves.
He said: Calves among the vines?

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי אִיקְּלַע לְגַבְלָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new story in the same series about the land's fruit.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why are calves standing among the vines?

steps.title: They are grape clusters
steps.stepSummary: The locals tell him that those are not calves; they are grape clusters.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to him: They are clusters.
steps.whatsHappening: The locals answer his question: what he saw were giant clusters of grapes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer reveals how large the fruit really was. This sets up his strong reaction in the next step.

phrases.english: They said to him: They are clusters.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers his question in step 7.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The 'calves' were really giant grape clusters.

steps.title: Land, hold back your fruit from the gentiles
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע בן לוי cries out to the land to take back its fruit, since it is only going to the גוים who rule over ישראל because of their sins.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said: Land, land, take in your fruit! For whom are you bringing out your fruit? For these gentiles who stand over us because of our sins?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהושע בן לוי speaks to the land itself and asks it to stop giving such great fruit, because the גוים are the ones enjoying it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Instead of being happy at the huge clusters, he is pained. Because of ישראל's sins, foreign rulers control the land and get its fruit, so he prefers that the land hold it back.
steps.whatToRemember: The land's blessing is meant for ישראל. When sin causes others to rule the land, its full fruit is not a cause for celebration.

phrases.english: He said: Land, land, take in your fruit!
For whom are you bringing out your fruit?
For these gentiles
who stand over us because of our sins?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: His reaction after learning that the 'calves' were clusters.
steps.whyThisMatters: Like רבי אלעזר's story, it ties the land's fruit to the spiritual state of ישראל.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Better that the land hold back its fruit than give it to foreign rulers who rule because of ישראל's sins.

steps.title: The next year, רבי חייא sees grape clusters like goats
steps.stepSummary: A year later רבי חייא visits the same place, sees clusters as big as goats, and asks if goats are standing among the vines.
steps.simpleTranslation: The next year, רבי חייא came to that place. He saw the clusters standing like goats and said: Goats among the vines?
steps.whatsHappening: A new visitor, רבי חייא, comes to the same vineyard a year later and asks the same kind of question רבי יהושע בן לוי asked. This sets up the locals' answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Last time the clusters looked like calves; now they look like goats, which are smaller. The size drop shows that רבי יהושע בן לוי's outcry from step 9 had already taken effect.

phrases.english: The next year, Rabbi Chiya happened to come there,
phrases.notes: "There" means Gavla, the same place רבי יהושע בן לוי visited in step 7.

phrases.english: he saw them (the clusters) standing like goats,
He said: Goats among the vines?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the Gavla story one year after רבי יהושע בן לוי's outcry, following the same pattern as step 7.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why are goats standing among the vines?

steps.title: The locals tell רבי חייא to leave so he won't curse them too
steps.stepSummary: The locals tell רבי חייא to go away and not do to them what his colleague did.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to him: Go away! Don't do to us what your friend did.
steps.whatsHappening: The locals answer רבי חייא by asking him to leave. They are afraid he will make the fruit shrink even more, as happened last time.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The locals blame the shrinking grapes on רבי יהושע בן לוי's words. Their answer confirms that the fruit really did shrink because of his outcry.
steps.whatToRemember: The fruit shrank from calf-size to goat-size within one year. The locals blamed רבי יהושע בן לוי's outcry for the drop.

phrases.english: They said to him: Go away,
don't do to us like your friend did.
phrases.notes: "Your friend" is רבי יהושע בן לוי, whose cry in step 9 made the fruit shrink.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי חייא's question in step 10.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The locals ask him to leave so he will not shrink the fruit further, as his colleague did.

steps.title: ארץ ישראל yields fifty thousand כור, while צוען yields seventy
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that in blessed times a בית סאה in ארץ ישראל produces fifty thousand כור, while in settled צוען it produces only seventy כור.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: When ארץ ישראל is blessed, one בית סאה of land produces fifty thousand כור. When צוען was settled, one בית סאה produced seventy כור.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא comparing how much grain the same amount of land produces in ארץ ישראל and in צוען, a rich area of מצרים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The point is the enormous gap: fifty thousand compared to seventy. The best farmland outside ארץ ישראל cannot come close to ארץ ישראל when it is blessed.

keyTerms.meaning: An area of land big enough to sow one סאה of seed
A large measure of grain (thirty סאה)
Zoan, a fertile region in מצרים

phrases.aramaic: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: בְּבִרְכוֹתֶיהָ שֶׁל אֶרֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל
phrases.english: The Rabbis taught: In the blessings of Eretz Yisrael,

phrases.aramaic: בֵּית סְאָה עוֹשָׂה חֲמֵשֶׁת רִיבּוֹא כּוֹרִין,
phrases.english: one beit se'a produces fifty thousand kor,
when Zoan was settled,
one beit se'a produced seventy kor.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: בְּבִרְכוֹתֶיהָ שֶׁל אֶרֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from stories to a ברייתא that measures the blessing of ארץ ישראל in numbers.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Blessed ארץ ישראל yields fifty thousand כור per בית סאה, while the best of מצרים yields seventy.

steps.title: רבי מאיר saw seventy כור per בית סאה in בית שאן
steps.stepSummary: Support from a ברייתא: רבי מאיר testifies that he saw a בית סאה in the valley of בית שאן produce seventy כור.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught: רבי מאיר said: I saw in the valley of בית שאן that one בית סאה produced seventy כור.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא backs up the figure of seventy כור with an eyewitness report from רבי מאיר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The seventy-כור number is not made up. רבי מאיר personally saw excellent farmland produce exactly that amount, which shows the figure for צוען is realistic.

keyTerms.meaning: As it was taught (in a ברייתא)

phrases.english: As it was taught: Rabbi Meir said:
I saw in the valley of Beit She'an
one beit se'a producing seventy kor.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the seventy-כור figure from step 12.
steps.raayaObject: That a בית סאה of excellent land yields seventy כור.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי מאיר's eyewitness report from the valley of בית שאן.

steps.title: מצרים is the best land, and צוען is the best part of מצרים
steps.stepSummary: No land is better than מצרים, as the פסוק compares it to ה׳'s garden. Within מצרים, צוען is the best, since kings were raised there.
steps.simpleTranslation: No land is better than מצרים, as it says: "Like the garden of ה׳, like the land of מצרים." And no place in מצרים is better than צוען, because they raised kings there, as it is written: "For his princes were in צוען."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up a comparison. First it shows that צוען is the very best land anywhere outside ארץ ישראל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two פסוקים build the point step by step. מצרים is the best land, and צוען is the best spot in מצרים, since kings were raised there. So צוען is the top of the scale.

phrases.english: And there is none more excellent among all the lands
than the land of Egypt,
as it is stated: "Like the garden of ה׳, like the land of Egypt."

phrases.aramaic: וְאֵין לְךָ מְעוּלָּה בְּכׇל אֶרֶץ מִצְרַיִם יוֹתֵר מִצּוֹעַן
phrases.english: And there is none more excellent in all of Egypt than Zoan,
since they would raise kings there,
as it is written: "For his princes were in Zoan."

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאֵין לְךָ מְעוּלָּה בְּכׇל אֲרָצוֹת יוֹתֵר מֵאֶרֶץ מִצְרַיִם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds up צוען as the best land outside ארץ ישראל, preparing the comparison with חברון.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: צוען is the best spot in the best land, מצרים.

steps.title: חברון is the rockiest place in ארץ ישראל
steps.stepSummary: No place in ארץ ישראל is rockier than חברון, which is why people used it to bury their dead.
steps.simpleTranslation: And no place in all of ארץ ישראל is rockier than חברון, because people would bury the dead there.
steps.whatsHappening: Now the גמרא sets up the other side of the comparison. חברון is the worst farmland in ארץ ישראל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Using the rocky land for graves shows it was not good for farming. So the comparison will be the worst of ארץ ישראל against the best of the outside world.

phrases.aramaic: וְאֵין לְךָ טְרָשִׁים בְּכׇל אֶרֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל
phrases.english: And there is no rockier ground in all of Eretz Yisrael
than Hebron,
since they would bury the dead there.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאֵין לְךָ טְרָשִׁים בְּכׇל אֶרֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposite side of the comparison: the worst land in ארץ ישראל.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: חברון is the rockiest, least fertile place in ארץ ישראל.

steps.title: Even so, חברון was seven times better than צוען
steps.stepSummary: Despite being rocky, חברון was seven times more developed than צוען, based on the פסוק that חברון was 'built seven years before צוען.'
steps.simpleTranslation: And even so, חברון was seven times better developed than צוען, as it is written: "And חברון was built seven years before צוען of מצרים."
steps.whatsHappening: This is the punchline of the comparison. The worst place in ארץ ישראל beats the best place outside it seven times over.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא learns this from the words "seven years" in the פסוק. It reads them as a measure of quality, not time. The next steps explain why the פסוק can't mean this literally.
steps.whatToRemember: The rockiest part of ארץ ישראל (חברון) was seven times better than the finest land in the world outside it (צוען).

phrases.english: And even so,

phrases.aramaic: חֶבְרוֹן מְבוּנָּה עַל אַחַת מִשִּׁבְעָה בְּצוֹעַן,
phrases.english: Hebron was built up seven times more than Zoan,
phrases.notes: "Built up" here means fertile and productive, not just having buildings.

phrases.english: as it is written: "And Hebron was built seven years
before Zoan of Egypt."

steps.triggerLanguage: וַאֲפִילּוּ הָכִי, חֶבְרוֹן מְבוּנָּה עַל אַחַת מִשִּׁבְעָה בְּצוֹעַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the comparison set up in steps 14 and 15.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: חברון was sevenfold more fertile than צוען.

steps.title: What does 'was built' mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the word נבנתה in the פסוק means.
steps.simpleTranslation: What does "was built" mean?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא stops to ask what the word נבנתה really means in the פסוק. This sets up the next move.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof in step 16 only works if נבנתה is about fertility and not about actual construction. So the גמרא has to check what the word means.

phrases.english: What does "was built" mean?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the key word of the פסוק quoted in step 16.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The meaning of נבנתה in the פסוק.

steps.title: It can't mean literally built, since מצרים was older than כנען
steps.stepSummary: If נבנתה meant actual building, it makes no sense: a father would not build for his younger son (כנען) before his older son (מצרים), and the פסוק lists מצרים before כנען.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say it was literally built, would a person build a house for his younger son before building one for his older son? As it says: "And the sons of חם: כוש, and מצרים, and פוט, and כנען"!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the literal meaning of נבנתה. This clears the way for its own explanation, which comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: מצרים is listed before כנען, so he was the older son, and חברון is in כנען's land. It would be strange to build the younger son's city first. So נבנתה must mean something else, which supports reading it as fertility.

keyTerms.meaning: His younger son / his older son

steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא is not saying the פסוק is wrong. It is only rejecting the literal reading of נבנתה, to show that the word means something else.

phrases.english: If you say it was literally built,

phrases.aramaic: אֶפְשָׁר אָדָם בּוֹנֶה בַּיִת לִבְנוֹ קָטָן
phrases.english: is it possible that a person builds a house for his younger son
before he builds for his older son?
As it is stated: "And the sons of Ham:
Cush, and Mitzrayim, and Put, and Canaan"!
phrases.notes: בראשית 10:6. מצרים is listed before כנען, so he was older, and חברון is in כנען's land.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the most obvious answer to the question in step 17.
steps.kashyaTarget: The literal reading of נבנתה as physical construction.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: מצרים was older than כנען, as shown by the order in בראשית 10:6. A father would not build the younger son's city first, so חברון could not have been literally built before צוען.

steps.title: Built means more fertile, seven times over
steps.stepSummary: נבנתה does not mean physical building. It means חברון was seven times more developed and fertile than צוען.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it means that חברון was developed seven times more than צוען.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the problem from the last step by reading 'built' as 'developed and fertile,' not 'constructed.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 18 showed that literal building does not work, since a father would not build for the younger son first. So the פסוק is about quality: even rocky חברון produced seven times what the best land of מצרים produced.

phrases.english: Rather, it means that it was developed
sevenfold more than צוען.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא שֶׁמְּבוּנָּה עַל אַחַת מִשִּׁבְעָה בְּצוֹעֵן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the difficulty raised in step 18
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpretation of a word in the פסוק
steps.terutzHavaAmina: נבנתה means חברון was physically built before צוען
steps.terutzMaskana: נבנתה means חברון was seven times more fertile than צוען

steps.title: Non-rocky land produced even more
steps.stepSummary: The sevenfold figure is only for rocky land like חברון. Land that was not rocky produced up to five hundred.
steps.simpleTranslation: And this is only for rocky land. But land that was not rocky produced five hundred.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds that חברון's sevenfold yield was the low end. Regular, non-rocky land in ארץ ישראל produced even more.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 15 said חברון was the rockiest place in ארץ ישראל. If even the worst land beat the best of מצרים seven times over, better land did far better, and the גמרא puts it at five hundred.

keyTerms.meaning: And this applies only to (limits a rule)

phrases.english: And this applies only to rocky land,
but land that is not rocky: five hundred.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits step 19's figure to rocky land and gives a higher figure for good land
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Sevenfold is for rocky land. Non-rocky land of ארץ ישראל produced five hundred.

steps.title: In a blessed year, a hundred times more
steps.stepSummary: Even five hundred is for an ordinary year. In a blessed year the land gave a hundred times more, as with יצחק.
steps.simpleTranslation: And this is only when the land is not in its blessed state. But when it is blessed, it is written: 'And יצחק sowed in that land' (and found a hundredfold).
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes up one more level: in a year of blessing, the yield multiplies a hundred times, shown by the פסוק about יצחק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are three levels: rocky land (sevenfold over צוען), good land (five hundred), and good land in a blessed year (a hundred times that). The proof is יצחק's field, which gave a hundredfold.

keyTerms.meaning: In its blessed state, a year of blessing

steps.whatToRemember: Three levels of fertility: rocky חברון beat צוען sevenfold, good land gave five hundred, and in a blessed year a hundred times more, like יצחק's harvest.

phrases.english: And this applies only when it is not blessed,
but when it is blessed, it is written:
'And Isaac sowed in that land, etc.'
phrases.notes: בראשית 26:12. The rest of the פסוק says he found a hundredfold that year, and that is the point.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Raises the figure of step 20 for a blessed year
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In a blessed year the land produced a hundred times more, proven from יצחק's harvest.

steps.title: One סאה in יהודה gave five
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי teaches that a סאה of wheat in יהודה produced five סאין of different kinds of flour and bran.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: רבי יוסי said, a סאה in יהודה produced five סאין: a סאה of flour, a סאה of fine flour, a סאה of bran, a סאה of coarse bran, and a סאה of low-grade flour.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא with another example of the land's richness: grain from יהודה was so full that it ground into five times its volume.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the blessing is in each grain, not in the size of the harvest. One סאה of wheat yielded five full סאין of products, from the best flour down to the coarsest.

keyTerms.meaning: It was taught in a ברייתא

phrases.english: It was taught: Rabbi Yosei said:

phrases.aramaic: סְאָה בִּיהוּדָה הָיְתָה עוֹשָׂה חָמֵשׁ סְאִין:
phrases.english: A se'a in Judea would produce five se'a:
phrases.notes: He means one סאה of wheat, once ground.

phrases.english: a se'a of flour, a se'a of fine flour,
a se'a of bran, a se'a of coarse bran,
and a se'a of low-grade flour.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new source on the same theme of the land's fertility
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A סאה of wheat in יהודה yielded five סאין of flour products.

steps.title: A צדוקי praises his small field
steps.stepSummary: A צדוקי tells רבי חנינא that the praise is well earned: from one small field he gets oil, wine, grain, legumes, and grazing for his animals.
steps.simpleTranslation: A certain צדוקי said to רבי חנינא: You do well to praise your land. My father left me one בית סאה, and from it I get oil, wine, grain, legumes, and from it my flocks graze.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story in which even a צדוקי, an opponent of the חכמים, agrees that ארץ ישראל deserves its praise.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A בית סאה is a small plot, yet it gave him four kinds of produce (oil, wine, grain and legumes) plus pasture for his flocks. The praise carries extra weight because it comes from an outsider who has no reason to flatter the חכמים.

keyTerms.meaning: A Sadducee, a member of a group that rejected the חכמים
You praise well, the praise is fitting
An area of land sown with one סאה of seed (a small field)

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ הָהוּא צַדּוּקִי לְרַבִּי חֲנִינָא:
phrases.english: A certain Sadducee said to Rabbi Ḥanina:
You do well in praising your land.

phrases.aramaic: בֵּית סְאָה אַחַת הִנִּיחַ לִי אַבָּא,
phrases.english: My father left me one beit se'a of land,
from it oil, from it wine,
from it grain, from it legumes,
and from it my livestock graze.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ הָהוּא צַדּוּקִי לְרַבִּי חֲנִינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another story praising the land, now from an outsider
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One small field in ארץ ישראל supplied oil, wine, grain, legumes, and pasture.

steps.title: How much does the palm tree by the ירדן give?
steps.stepSummary: A man of the אמורי nation asks a resident of ארץ ישראל how much fruit they pick from a certain palm tree on the bank of the ירדן.
steps.simpleTranslation: A certain man of the אמורי people said to a man from ארץ ישראל: That palm tree standing on the bank of the ירדן, how much do you pick from it?
steps.whatsHappening: A new story begins. The אמורי asks a question that sets up a comparison between how much the tree gives now and how much it gave in his people's time.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The אמורים lived in the land before the Jews. This question opens a back-and-forth that ends by showing how rich the land still is.

keyTerms.meaning: A man of the אמורי nation
On the bank of the ירדן

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ הָהוּא בַּר אֱמוֹרָאָה לְבַר אַרְעָא דְיִשְׂרָאֵל:
phrases.english: A certain Amorite said to a resident of Eretz Yisrael:
That palm tree which stands on the bank of the Jordan,
phrases.notes: The word in square brackets is the corrected wording, and it means 'palm tree.'

phrases.english: how much do you pick from it?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ הָהוּא בַּר אֱמוֹרָאָה לְבַר אַרְעָא דְיִשְׂרָאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new story on the same theme
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How much fruit the palm tree by the ירדן yields

steps.title: Sixty כור
steps.stepSummary: The resident answers that they pick sixty כור of dates from the tree.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Sixty כור.
steps.whatsHappening: The resident gives his answer: sixty כור, a huge amount for a single tree.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Sixty כור is already an enormous yield. The Amorite will now use this number to complain that the land has declined.

keyTerms.meaning: כור measures (a large unit, thirty סאין)

phrases.english: He said to him: Sixty kor.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 24

steps.title: The אמורי: You have already ruined it
steps.stepSummary: The אמורי complains that the Jews have barely settled the land and already ruined it, since his people picked 120 כור from that tree.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: You have not yet even entered it, and you have already destroyed it! We used to pick 120 כור from it.
steps.whatsHappening: The אמורי challenges the resident: sixty כור is only half of what his people used to get, so the land must have gotten worse.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He compares the two numbers, 60 against 120, and concludes that the land lost half its blessing under Jewish settlement. The resident still has to answer this attack.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: אַכַּתִּי לָא עָיְילִיתוּ בָּהּ
phrases.english: He said to him: You have not yet entered it,
and you have destroyed it.
We, one hundred and twenty kor
we used to pick from it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: אַכַּתִּי לָא עָיְילִיתוּ בָּהּ אַחְרֵיבְתּוּהָ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the answer of step 25 to attack
steps.kashyaTarget: The resident's figure of sixty כור
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The אמורים picked 120 כור, so 60 means the land has declined by half

steps.title: That was only one side of the tree
steps.stepSummary: The resident answers that his sixty כור were from just one side of the tree, so the full yield is the same 120.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: I too was telling you only about one side.
steps.whatsHappening: The resident answers the complaint: he only counted one side of the tree, so the land has not lost anything.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The אמורי's attack depended on sixty being the whole yield. Once we hear it was half the tree, the total matches the old 120 כור, and the land's blessing is shown to be unchanged.
steps.whatToRemember: The palm tree story ends by showing the land's blessing was unchanged: sixty כור from one side means 120 in total, just like in the אמורים' days.

phrases.english: He said to him: I too
was speaking to you about only one side.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: אֲנָא נָמֵי מֵחַד גִּיסָא קָאָמֵינָא לָךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the attack of step 26
steps.terutzResolutionType: Clarifying the scope of the earlier answer
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Sixty כור was the whole tree's yield, so the land declined
steps.terutzMaskana: Sixty כור was from one side only, so the total still equals 120

steps.title: Why the land is called a deer: its fruit overflows
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא asks why ירמיהו compares ארץ ישראל to a צבי. He answers that a deer's skin cannot hold its meat, and the land likewise cannot hold all its fruit.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said: What does the פסוק mean, 'And I will give you a desirable land, an inheritance of a צבי'? Why is ארץ ישראל compared to a deer? To teach you that just as a deer's skin cannot hold its meat, so ארץ ישראל cannot hold all its fruit.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא opens a new teaching. He takes a word in a פסוק, צבי (deer), and explains what it teaches about ארץ ישראל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once a deer is skinned, the skin looks too small to wrap the meat again. רב חסדא says ארץ ישראל is the same: once its fruit is picked, the land seems too small to hold it all. The point is that the harvest is huge.

keyTerms.meaning: Deer. Also used as a word of beauty, as in 'the inheritance of a צבי'

phrases.english: Rav Chisda said,
What is the meaning of what is written:
"And I will give you a desirable land, an inheritance of a deer"?
Why is Eretz Yisrael compared to a deer?
To tell you:

phrases.aramaic: מָה צְבִי זֶה אֵין עוֹרוֹ מַחֲזִיק בְּשָׂרוֹ,
phrases.english: Just as this deer, its skin cannot hold its meat,

phrases.aramaic: אַף אֶרֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל אֵינָהּ מַחְזֶקֶת פֵּירוֹתֶיהָ.
phrases.english: so too Eretz Yisrael cannot hold its fruit.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the theme of the land's huge fertility from the palm tree story, now through a פסוק.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: ארץ ישראל is compared to a צבי because its fruit is too plentiful for the land to hold, just as a deer's skin cannot hold its meat.

steps.title: A second explanation: the land ripens fruit quickly
steps.stepSummary: A second reading of the comparison: the deer is the fastest animal, and ארץ ישראל ripens its fruit faster than any other land.
steps.simpleTranslation: Another explanation: just as the deer is the fastest of all animals, so ארץ ישראל is the fastest of all lands to ripen its fruit.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second, different meaning for the deer comparison.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first explanation was about how much fruit there is. This one is about speed: the deer is swift, and the land brings its fruit to ripeness quickly.

keyTerms.meaning: Here: to ripen fruit, not to cook

steps.confusionAlert: לבשל usually means 'to cook', but here it means the land ripens its fruit quickly.

phrases.english: Another explanation:

phrases.aramaic: מָה צְבִי זֶה קַל מִכׇּל הַחַיּוֹת,
phrases.english: Just as this deer is swifter than all the animals,

phrases.aramaic: אַף אֶרֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל קַלָּה מִכׇּל הָאֲרָצוֹת
phrases.english: so too Eretz Yisrael is swifter than all the lands
to ripen its fruit.

steps.triggerLanguage: דָּבָר אַחֵר: מָה צְבִי זֶה קַל מִכׇּל הַחַיּוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a second meaning for the same comparison.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: ארץ ישראל ripens its fruit faster than any other land, like the swift deer.

steps.title: Challenge: does the comparison mean the fruit is lean?
steps.stepSummary: If ארץ ישראל is like a deer, maybe the comparison goes further. A deer is fast but its meat is lean, so perhaps the land's fruit ripens fast but is not rich.
steps.simpleTranslation: But maybe: just as a deer is swift but its meat is not fatty, so ארץ ישראל ripens fruit quickly but its fruit is not rich and juicy?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes the deer comparison further to see if it leads to a bad conclusion about the land's fruit.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Comparisons can carry more than we want. A deer is fast, but it is also lean. If the land is fully like a deer, its fruit might be fast-growing but thin and dry.

phrases.english: If so, just as this deer is swift
and its meat is not fatty,
so too Eretz Yisrael is swift to ripen
but its fruit is not rich?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי מָה צְבִי זֶה קַל וְאֵין בְּשָׂרוֹ שָׁמֵן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the second explanation by extending the comparison.
steps.kashyaTarget: The comparison of ארץ ישראל to a swift deer.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the land is like a deer in speed, it might also be like a deer in leanness, so its fruit would not be rich.

steps.title: Answer: the fruit is richer than milk and sweeter than honey
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק 'זבת חלב ודבש' shows the fruit is rich and sweet, so the deer comparison stops at speed.
steps.simpleTranslation: That is why the פסוק says 'flowing with milk and honey': the fruit is richer than milk and sweeter than honey.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by bringing a different פסוק about the land.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Another פסוק describes the land as flowing with milk and honey. This tells us the fruit is rich and sweet. So the deer comparison only teaches speed, not leanness.

keyTerms.meaning: That is why the פסוק says

steps.whatToRemember: ארץ ישראל is like a deer in speed: its fruit ripens fast and is plentiful. But it is not like a deer in leanness, because its fruit is rich like milk and sweet like honey.

phrases.english: The verse teaches:
"Flowing with milk and honey";
richer than milk and sweeter than honey.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 30.
steps.terutzResolutionType: A second פסוק limits the comparison
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The deer comparison might mean the fruit is lean.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'זבת חלב ודבש' shows the fruit is rich and sweet, so the comparison is only about speed.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר celebrates escaping one, two, then three curses
steps.stepSummary: When רבי אלעזר moved to ארץ ישראל, received סמיכה, and joined the סוד העיבור, he each time said he had escaped one more curse.
steps.simpleTranslation: When רבי אלעזר went up to ארץ ישראל, he said: I escaped one. When they gave him סמיכה, he said: I escaped two. When they seated him in the סוד העיבור, he said: I escaped three.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story about רבי אלעזר and the three stages he celebrated. This step sets up the next step, which explains which curses he means.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each stage was a new honor: living in the land, being ordained, and joining the group that sets the calendar. He saw each one as escaping a curse, but the curses are only identified in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: The council that adds a month to the year and sets the calendar

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר כִּי הֲוָה סָלֵיק לְאֶרֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל,
phrases.english: When Rabbi Elazar went up to Eretz Yisrael,
he said: I have escaped one.
phrases.notes: He means one curse. The next step tells us which ones.

phrases.english: When they ordained him,
he said: I have escaped two.
When they seated him in the council for adding a month to the year,
he said: I have escaped three,

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר כִּי הֲוָה סָלֵיק לְאֶרֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new story continuing the theme of the greatness of ארץ ישראל.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי אלעזר saw living in ארץ ישראל, receiving סמיכה, and joining the סוד העיבור as three escapes from curses.

steps.title: The source: three curses on false prophets in יחזקאל
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק in יחזקאל curses false prophets with three things. They will not be in the סוד העיבור, will not receive סמיכה, and will not enter ארץ ישראל.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it says: 'My hand will be against the prophets who see falsehood...' 'They will not be in the council of My people' means the סוד העיבור. 'They will not be written in the record of the house of Israel' means סמיכה. 'They will not come to the land of Israel' means just what it says.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the פסוק that explains the three curses רבי אלעזר was talking about.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק lists three punishments for false prophets. The גמרא matches each one to a stage in רבי אלעזר's life. Since he received all three blessings, he knew none of these curses applied to him.

keyTerms.meaning: As it sounds, the plain meaning
And so on, the פסוק continues

steps.whatToRemember: The three curses in יחזקאל are: no place in the סוד העיבור, no סמיכה, and no entry into ארץ ישראל. רבי אלעזר escaped all three, one at a time.

phrases.english: as it is stated:

phrases.aramaic: ״וְהָיְתָה יָדִי אֶל הַנְּבִיאִים הַחוֹזִים שָׁוְא וְגוֹ׳״.
phrases.english: "And My hand shall be against the prophets who see falsehood, etc."
phrases.notes: יחזקאל 13:9. The 'etc.' means the פסוק continues with the three parts quoted next.

phrases.english: "They shall not be in the council of My people":
this is the council for adding a month to the year.
"Nor shall they be written in the record of the house of Israel":
this is ordination.
"Nor shall they come to the land of Israel":
as it sounds.

steps.triggerLanguage: שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: וְהָיְתָה יָדִי אֶל הַנְּבִיאִים הַחוֹזִים שָׁוְא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source for the three curses mentioned in step 32.
steps.raayaObject: רבי אלעזר's statement that he escaped three curses.
steps.raayaSupportSource: יחזקאל 13:9, read as three curses: no סוד העיבור, no סמיכה, no entry into ארץ ישראל.

steps.title: רבי זירא crosses the river on a rope
steps.stepSummary: On his way to ארץ ישראל, רבי זירא found no ferry, so he held onto a rope and crossed the river.
steps.simpleTranslation: When רבי זירא was going up to ארץ ישראל, he could not find a ferry to cross the river. So he grabbed a rope and crossed on it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new story about רבי זירא's trip to ארץ ישראל. He was in such a hurry that he crossed the river on a rope.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Crossing on a rope is hard and risky, and waiting for a ferry would have been the normal thing to do. His rush shows how badly he wanted to reach the land. It also sets up the mocking question that comes next.

keyTerms.meaning: A ferry, a boat for crossing a river
A rope stretched across the river

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי זֵירָא כִּי הֲוָה סָלֵיק לְאֶרֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל
phrases.english: When Rabbi Zeira was going up to Eretz Yisrael
he did not find a ferry to cross,
phrases.notes: The river here is the ירדן.

phrases.english: so he held onto a rope and crossed.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי זֵירָא כִּי הֲוָה סָלֵיק לְאֶרֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another story of a חכם's love for ארץ ישראל, following רבי אלעזר's joy at arriving there.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי זירא was so eager to reach ארץ ישראל that he crossed the river on a rope instead of waiting for a ferry.

steps.title: A צדוקי mocks רבי זירא as hasty
steps.stepSummary: A צדוקי mocks רבי זירא, saying the Jews have always been hasty, ever since they said נעשה before נשמע.
steps.simpleTranslation: A certain צדוקי said to him: You hasty people! You put your mouths before your ears, and you are still just as hasty!
steps.whatsHappening: A צדוקי sees רבי זירא crossing on the rope and makes fun of him. He says this rushing is typical of the Jewish people.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He means that at הר סיני the Jews said 'we will do' before 'we will hear', promising before listening. He calls that reckless, and says crossing a river on a rope instead of waiting is the same old rashness.

keyTerms.meaning: A Sadducee, someone who rejected the חכמים

phrases.english: A certain Sadducee said to him:
Hasty people!
who put your mouths before your ears,
phrases.notes: He means נַעֲשֶׂה וְנִשְׁמָע, saying 'we will do' before 'we will hear'. See שמות 24:7.

phrases.english: you are still in your hastiness?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רבי זירא's rushed crossing from the previous step.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי זירא's rush to cross the river on a rope
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Rushing without waiting for a proper ferry is rash, just like promising to obey before hearing the commands.

steps.title: רבי זירא: even משה and אהרן did not merit this land
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא answers that משה and אהרן never got to enter ארץ ישראל, so he could not be sure he would. He did not want to risk delay.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: A place that משה and אהרן did not merit to enter, who can say that I will merit it?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא answers the צדוקי. His rush was not rashness. He was afraid of losing the chance to enter the land.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If even משה and אהרן were stopped from entering ארץ ישראל, entering is clearly a special privilege. Waiting even a little might let something get in the way, so hurrying was the wise choice.
steps.whatToRemember: רבי זירא rushed because entering ארץ ישראל is a privilege that even משה and אהרן did not receive.

phrases.english: He said to him:

phrases.aramaic: דּוּכְתָּא דְּמֹשֶׁה וְאַהֲרֹן לָא זְכוֹ לַהּ,
phrases.english: A place that Moshe and Aharon did not merit,
as for me, who can say that I will merit it?

steps.triggerLanguage: דּוּכְתָּא דְּמֹשֶׁה וְאַהֲרֹן לָא זְכוֹ לַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the צדוקי's mocking challenge.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Recasting the action: the haste was careful worry about missing out, not recklessness.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Crossing on a rope looks like careless hurry.
steps.terutzMaskana: Since even משה and אהרן never entered, any delay could cost him the privilege, so hurrying was wise.

steps.title: רבי אבא kisses the rocks of עכו
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבא would kiss the rocks of עכו out of love for ארץ ישראל.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבא would kiss the rocks of עכו.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives another short example of a חכם's love for the land. רבי אבא kissed its stones.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even the plain rocks of ארץ ישראל were precious to him. This adds one more picture to the list of how the חכמים showed love for the land.

keyTerms.meaning: Akko, a city of ארץ ישראל

phrases.english: Rabbi Abba would kiss the rocks of Akko.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds another חכם to the list of those who showed love for ארץ ישראל.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי אבא showed his love for the land by kissing its rocks.

steps.title: רבי חנינא repairs the land's stumbling blocks
steps.stepSummary: רבי חנינא would fix the land's stumbling blocks, the places where people might trip.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חנינא would fix its stumbling blocks.
steps.whatsHappening: Another example of love for the land. רבי חנינא repaired places where people might trip.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He did not only admire the land, he took care of it. Fixing the dangerous spots kept people from getting hurt and complaining about ארץ ישראל.

keyTerms.meaning: Its stumbling blocks, places where people trip

phrases.english: Rabbi Chanina would fix its stumbling blocks.
phrases.notes: 'Its' means the land's, like holes and bumps in the roads.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the list of חכמים who showed love for the land.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי חנינא showed his love for the land by repairing its hazards.

steps.title: Opening of the story about רבי אמי and רבי אסי
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins one more example, about רבי אמי and רבי אסי. The sentence continues on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אמי and רבי אסי...
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. The גמרא starts naming the next pair of חכמים, and what they did comes on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This continues the same list of love for ארץ ישראל. Only the names appear here, so wait for the rest of the sentence to see what they did.

keyTerms.meaning: Rabbi Ammi, an אמורא of ארץ ישראל

phrases.english: Rabbi Ammi and Rabbi Asi

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts the next item in the list of חכמים who loved the land.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Introduces רבי אמי and רבי אסי as the next example. The rest follows.
